learningObjectives: Select and justify connectors and services in a business scenario.
Select and justify external data sources for data types in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

topics.title: External data sources for data types

elements.description: A connector lets Pega call an external system; a service lets an external caller invoke Pega. Choose the direction first, then protocol, authentication, mapping and failure behavior. SOAP uses a WSDL contract; REST integrations use HTTP resources and operations.

elements.text: Worked example: A claim needs a repair estimate from a vendor: Pega calls the vendor with a connector. If the vendor creates a claim in Pega, the inbound request uses a Pega service/API.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: External data sources for data types

elements.description: A Data Type can use a local Pega system of record, transient case data, or an external source. External-source configuration creates connector and mapping assets. Parameterize requests, map response fields, use authentication profiles and vary endpoints by environment rather than copying hard-coded production URLs.

elements.text: Worked example: A D_Customer page passes CustomerID to a REST service and maps the returned name and contact fields. Test Dev and Production endpoint settings and reject a mismatched response.

items.label: External data sources for data types

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Direction
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A connector exposes a Pega API to external callers.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Connectors call out; services receive calls.

examPitfalls.title: Transport versus mapping
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A successful HTTP call proves all fields are mapped correctly.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Assert the mapped values and error paths.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Pega must call a warehouse API to obtain stock. Which integration direction applies?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The application is the caller of an external system, so it uses a connector.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A supplier must create a case in Pega from its own application. Which direction applies?

options.text: A connector used only for outbound requests
A Pega service/API receiving the request

practiceQuiz.rationale: An external client invokes Pega through an inbound service/API. An outbound connector serves the opposite direction.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A legacy SOAP endpoint describes its operations and messages. Which artifact provides that contract?
practiceQuiz.rationale: WSDL describes the SOAP service interface and is used when configuring operations and mappings.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO belong in an integration design before declaring it ready?

options.text: A guarantee that timeouts cannot occur

practiceQuiz.rationale: A reachable endpoint is not enough. Authentication, correct mappings and explicit error handling make the integration usable.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A customer ID changes between calls. How should a reusable data source identify the requested customer?

options.text: Pass the customer ID as a request parameter
Create a new connector rule for every customer
Use the case urgency as the ID

practiceQuiz.rationale: Parameterization supports reuse while selecting the correct source record.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A data object exists only while a case is processed and is not pushed to a system of record. Which source classification fits?

options.text: External system of record by definition
A SOAP operation regardless of use

practiceQuiz.rationale: Not all application data is persisted to a system of record. Transient processing data can use this source classification.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The same integration is moved from QA to Production. Which configuration prevents calls to the QA endpoint?
practiceQuiz.rationale: External resource addresses can differ by environment. Configuration must select the target environment's endpoint.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A REST call returns HTTP success but the customer name is empty in Pega. What should be examined?

options.text: Response mapping and actual payload structure

practiceQuiz.rationale: Successful transport does not establish correct field mapping. Inspect the payload, nesting and mapping rules.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
